ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Speaking Fluency: pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

2. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

3. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library
   D. where is the library

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

6. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. happiness

7. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

9. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

10. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

12. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)

14. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)

15. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. goes
   C. going
   D. went
